title_original: Case 137 review – tense gilets-jaunes thriller divides cop’s loyalties over police brutality
editorial_title_zh: 《137号卷宗》影评——紧张的“黄马甲”惊悚片让警察在面对警察暴力时陷入忠诚抉择
editorial_excerpt_zh: 多米尼克·摩尔（Dominik Moll）执导的一部紧凑、充满张力的程序片，讲述了一位内心矛盾的警官调查一名青少年抗议者遭受暴力事件的故事。多米尼克·摩尔的《137号卷宗》是一部关于法国警察暴力的严肃、专注却又略显公式化的电影；其中带有纪录剧风格的叙事反射……

"当斯黛芬妮意识到受伤男孩来自她的省级家乡圣迪济耶（Saint-Dizier，正是那种人们觉得被马克龙精英阶层抛弃的地方）时，她的生活变得更加复杂；当她回到那里探望母亲时，她面临着撞见男孩悲痛欲绝的母亲（桑德拉·科隆博饰）的风险。这种秘密的联系激发了斯黛芬妮的活力，她在寻找有罪警察并将其绳之以法的过程中变得更加强硬和执着——但可怕的真相是，现在她自己也在走捷径，甚至可能面临调查。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "影片最扎实的部分在于，它煞费苦心地——几乎以叙事中实时同步的方式——带我们经历寻找警察罪魁祸过的整个过程：通过查找袭击青少年现场的闭路电视画面，然后极其缓慢地寻找附近摄像机的其他视频，追踪罪魁祸首的路线，直到能够识别出违规警官。这一连串冷静的取证影像与如今已很常见、能使违规警察受到起诉的真实智能手机示威视频并置在一起。", "translated": true}, {"type": "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "归根结底，斯黛芬妮所面临的部落式忠诚冲突——巴黎与小镇之间、警察与自由派批评者之间——并没有导向任何非常具有挑战性的方向，这部电影远不如摩尔在2000年推出的、当年在戛纳大获成功的获奖心理正剧《哈里，来帮忙》那样复杂，但它是一部崇高且有价值的作品。", "translated": true}, article_text:
D ominik Moll’s Dossier 137 is a serious, focused, if slightly programmatic movie about police brutality in France; there are docu-dramatic storytelling reflexes and a determined procedural tread. The movie takes its cue from the horrifying real-life cases of gilets-jaunes protesters in France’s 2018 demonstrations who suffered near fatal injuries due to the police’s trigger-happy use of the LBD gun : the lanceur de balle de défense or “flash ball” gun which (deafeningly) fires vicious rubber bullets.

Stéphanie, played by Léa Drucker, is a conscientious police officer in the IGPN, the Inspection Générale de la Police Nationale, effectively the Internal Affairs bureau, investigating horrific head injuries suffered by a teen protester, which could only be caused by the cops’ flash-ball weapons. She is divorced from a cop, Jérémy (Stanislas Merhar) who along with his new girlfriend – also in the police – is gloweringly resentful of what he sees as her bureau’s disloyal undermining of the police, and the way she is questioning the corners they (supposedly) have to cut to keep France safe, especially after the Bataclan attacks .

Stéphanie’s life becomes even more complicated when she realises that the injured boy is from her provincial hometown, Saint-Dizier – exactly the kind of place where people feel left behind by the Macron elite – and when she goes back there to visit her mum, she is in danger of running into the boy’s own stricken mother (Sandra Colombo). The secret connection energises Stéphanie, she gets tougher and more persistent in her quest to find the guilty cop and put him away – but the awful truth is that now she is cutting her own corners and might get investigated herself.

The film is on its most solid ground when it painstakingly – almost in the narrative equivalent of real time – takes us through the process of locating the cop culprits by finding CCTV footage from the site of the attack on the teenagers and then agonisingly slowly finding other videos from cameras nearby, tracking the culprits’ route until the offending officers can be identified. This succession of coolly forensic images are juxtaposed with the kind of real smartphone demo footage that is now commonplace and which gets errant police officers prosecuted.

Stéphanie and her colleagues are convinced that cameras like this might be found in a luxury hotel whose rear entrance faces the crime scene – and this is to bring her into contact with a possible eyewitness: a hotel room cleaner, Alicia, played by Guslagie Malaga (best known for Alice Diop’s courtroom drama Saint Omer). Moll gives Stéphanie a rather stagey and melodramatic one-on-one scene with Alicia as she begs her to help, but Alicia says that putting her head over the parapet to criticise the cops will only get her into trouble – and if the injured teen wasn’t white, Stéphanie and her colleagues wouldn’t care anyway. It’s a bit overwrought and redundant, especially as Alicia’s evidence is in fact a smartphone video that can be simply made available to the police without Alicia needing to go on the record at all.

In the end, the issue of Stéphanie’s tribal conflicts of loyalty – between Paris and small town, between the cops and their liberal critics – doesn’t lead anywhere very challenging, and this film is nowhere near as complex as, say, Moll’s award-winning psychological drama Harry, He’s Here to Help from 2000, a big Cannes success in its day, but it’s high-minded, valuable work.

article_text:
Source: Paul Marc Mitchell

Carol Morley

Shooting within a 15-minute travel radius was one way of keeping costs down on Carol Morley’s Stockport-set coming-of-age story 7 Miles Out.

“Our central base was former council offices, and we didn’t have trucks, so that was our base for hair and makeup,” says the UK writer-director. “It was a 25-day shoot, and I had to get it all in those days. I couldn’t do reshoots or pickups.”

The film is making its world premiere at the BFI London Film Festival as the sole UK title in competition. Based on Morley’s 2015 novel of the same name and inspired by her youth in Stockport – seven miles from Manchester – 7 Miles Out follows a young woman navigating first love, friendship and grief after the death of her father. It is set against the 1980s Manchester music scene.

The novel was first published in 2015. Fellow UK filmmaker Michael Winterbottom was interviewing Morley during the pandemic for a book on UK independent filmmakers, when he suggested adapting it for screen.

“I’d excavated that part of my life, and it never occurred to me to do anything [further] with it,” says Morley. “I had to go back to those times in a deeper way. I went through this second amount of pain, to get to an authenticity and truth.”

7 Miles Out is the first of Morley’s films not to receive public funding from either the BFI or BBC Film, after films including Dreams Of A Life , The Falling and 2022’s Typist Artist Pirate King .

“Their money taught me how to be a filmmaker,” says Morley. “In this case, I’m pleased if newcomers got the money.”

That required hustling for private finance, which Morley has always been apt at doing. One meeting alongside her long-time producer Cairo Cannon with an unnamed potential financier sticks in her mind. “It was critical. We were already in prep in Stockport,” she recalls. “We’d planned everything we would and wouldn’t say… then we just went against all of that. We pigeonholed him on this sofa, and didn’t stop talking for 20 minutes about why this film was important.

“We’d agreed not to ask him [in the meeting] whether he would give us the money. And at the end we went, ‘Do you think you will give us the money?’ He said, ‘Yes, if you promise I never have to have a meeting with you again, because that was intense!’”

The UK tax credit also proved useful, “because you can get it before post, and then at the end. The shifts in the tax credit changed a lot for us.”

No shouting

As on The Falling , all of the HODs on 7 Miles Out were women, including cinematographer Agnes Godard, composer Carly Paradis, casting directors Shaheen Baig and Naomi Jalil, and rising editor Raluca Petre.

“It’s not something I’m conscious of,” says Morley, while acknowledging the rules she introduces for her sets. “There’s no shouting allowed. No demonstration of displeasure. I know what I want, but I’m always ready to listen to everybody and their input because that’s exciting. Then in the edit, working with a woman editor and composer. They’re bringing their experience of girlhood and womanhood to it.”

According to Morley, 7 Miles Out is one of the first feature films to have been shot in Stockport. “Things can be represented from the outside in; this is definitely an inside-out film,” says the filmmaker. “There’s a weird northern mentality; everyone thinks their hometown is crap but is very proud of it. The big T-shirts in Stockport now say ‘Stockport’s not shit’.”

Source: CAMP

‘7 Miles Out’

Lucy Halliday , a 2024 Screen UK-Ireland Star of Tomorrow, stars in the film alongside Gemma Whelan and Aidan Gillen, who play her parents. The majority of the rest of the cast came from the Stockport and Manchester area, to save on accommodation costs.

“That’s how we found [ The Falling actress] Florence Pugh, she was local to Oxford,” says Morley. “It was about, ‘How do we circumvent what costs money?’”

The soundtrack includes The Clash, The Fall, Magazine, and six Joy Division tracks (plus one by New Order). “There were something like 120 rights-holders, because different people have the rights,” says Morley. “Some of the more obscure tracks were the hardest to clear because people didn’t know who owned it anymore.”

The filmmaker already has a script for her next feature, a time-travelling lesbian witch romance titled Air Of Night . It follows two young women who travel back to 1650 to a place of ill repute in London.

“It’s a witch film, but there are different levels of witches,” says Morley. “There are those back in the day who weren’t witches but were accused; and then there are my contemporary young women who are taken back.”

Morley says the film has been written with cast in mind, with those discussions starting once she has finished another draft.

article_text:
Source: Getty Images for BFI

Aimee Lou Wood

UK actor Aimee Lou Wood said she had to “quieten her voice” early in her career and is still discouraged from speaking up on film sets.

“[You’re] having to hide how clever you are and how much you can see things and how you’re clocking absolutely everything,” Wood told Screen at the BFI London Film Festival premiere of The Idiot(s) on October 14.

“But you have to dilute that to make people feel comfortable because men have very fragile egos a lot of the time.”

The Idiot(s) sees Wood play Anna Dostoevskaya, a real 19 th -century Russian memoirist and wife to the famed author, Fyodor Dostoevsky.

“In this industry, there’s a lot of trying to be right and not be the one who got it wrong,” the actor continued. “Instead of working together and collaborating as us versus the problem, it becomes very hierarchical, and I just don’t get it.”

Wood said she was told she “should be afraid” to speak up on sets and to producers, when she believed everyone on set was equal.

“Sometimes I have found, not anymore but when I was younger, I had to tone down and quieten my voice basically,” the actor said.

Love for European cinema

The Idiot(s) is directed by Polish directors Małgorzata Szumowska and Michał Englert. Johnny Flynn and Vicky Krieps also star.

Krieps, who has worked in several Hollywood features, says she always comes back to European films.

“You will find me often in movies where I have very small parts, and that’s something I do to support European independent cinema,” Krieps told Screen . “I will always do that forever. It’s something I do very consciously.”

UK actor Flynn echoed Krieps’s thoughts on filmmaking in Europe as compared to the UK. “People can take bigger risks [in Europe],” he suggested. “It’s easier to get funding for a film like this. I’m not sure this would be made in the UK.”

Suggesting that restrictions to funding in the UK are to blame, Flynn continued: “There’s an auteur culture in Europe that perhaps serves a more interesting version of cinema than a by-the-numbers UK approach.

“But this is more an appeal to the government to release money, and the institutions that fund films, rather than a criticism of British filmmakers.”

Flynn also stars as theatre director Richard Eyre in Simon Stone’s LFF opening film Elsinore.

Spot the banana shark: 30 years of Bondi’s Sculpture by the Sea – in pictures

The stunning 2km Bondi to Tamarama coastal walk in Sydney’s east has again been transformed into a giant sculpture park. This year’s Sculpture by the Sea marks 30 years since the first exhibition in 1997. It has grown to become known as the world’s largest free outdoor sculpture exhibition. Here’s a look back at some favourite pieces

article_text:
ビックリするほど当たるためIMA御用達の占い師・マコが、12星座の今をタロット1枚で運気予報！フォトグラファー清水はるみによるファンタスティックな星座＆大アルカナのヴィジュアルと共に、明るい未来の指針を毎月前・後半でお届けします。

9月後半に思うこと

「瀬戸内グリーンレモンに恋した理由」

それは、滋賀の日吉大社、奈良の橿原神宮、そして天河大弁財天社を巡る聖地巡礼の旅から始まった。神聖な空気に触れ、心身が大きく震えた直後、私はなぜか「塩レモン」に強烈に取り憑かれることになったのだ。

気になって仕方がなくなり取り寄せたのは、今しか手に入らない瀬戸内のグリーンレモン「璃の香」。形はいびつで傷もある「訳ありレモン」だ。しかし、見栄えの良いエリートよりも、野生の生命力が詰まったその姿に愛おしさが爆発。さらにレモンの輪切りにローズマリーとバニラエッセンスを合わせて火にかけ、じっくりと煮出してみる。部屋中に広がるすっきりと鋭いハーブの香りと、すべてを包み込むような甘い香り。その贅沢な香りを胸いっぱいに吸い込んでいる時間が何より心地良かった。

実はこの衝動、単なる料理ブームではない。私は今、人間関係を軽くし、過去の恐怖を克服して、新しいことに挑戦したい！という人生の転換期に立っている。この時、私が出合えた3つの素材は、私の決意を支えるスピリチュアルメッセージが隠されていた。青々と香る「ローズマリー」は古来より「記憶」と「トラウマの解消」を司る聖なるハーブだ、過去の恐怖を整理しメンタルを強く保つための戦士のような強さを授けてくれる。鋭い光を放つ「レモン」は澱んだエネルギーを強烈に弾き飛ばす」邪気払い」の象徴。特に今回選んだ「グリーンレモン」はハートチャクラを癒やし、未熟な状態からステップアップする「リスタート」のサイン。最後に、甘く漂う「バニラ」は、過去の恐怖で傷つき、固くなっていた内なる子供の心（インナーチャイルド）を「もう大丈夫だよ」と優しく抱きしめる「絶対的な安心感と自愛」をもたらす。

過去の恐怖を克服しようとする時、心は大きなエネルギーを消費する。ローズマリーで過去を断ち切り、レモンで道を拓き、バニラで自分を最大に愛するという「魔法の調合」なのだ。そこに祓いの代表「塩」が加わり私は最強になれるのです！

自分で仕込んだ塩レモンを、玉ねぎセロリ麹、ニンニクと合わせて豚しゃぶでいただく夜。レモンが瓶の中でじっくりと発酵していくように私の新しい人生もまた、ここから力強く豊かに熟成を始めていく。ハズ……。

article_text:
Source: ome Film Fest/Dammicco

Tessa Ross at Rome Film Fest

Bafta-winning Conclave producer Tessa Ross sat down with friend, filmmaker and collaborator Edward Berger to reflect on their work together, the role of public funders in the UK and making independent films amid an increasingly challenging environment, for this year’s Paso Doble in-conversation at Rome Film Fest on October 14.

The anecdote-filled tête-à-tête explored what it means to be a filmmaker and a creative producer and how these relationships work. The event was led by curator, distributor and producer Nico Marzano.

Ross’s recent credits include the multiple-award-winning 2024 papal drama Conclave and Danny Boyle’s Venice premiere Ink through her House Productions outfit, set up after fruitful stints as the head of drama at the BBC and as director of Film4. She has executive producer credits on myriad era-defining UK films from Billy Ellio t, Slumdog Millionaire and The Last King Of Scotland to 12 Years A Slave , The Lobster , Carol and The Zone Of Interest .

“What makes me fall in love with the project is the people or the person behind it,” Ross revealed. “I wish there was a science, but there isn’t.”

She believes almost all stories can be told in many different ways by many different people. “But it is always the talent of a writer or a director or a writer-director, the vision of somebody very particular, an author that makes me think I have a place in that storytelling,” she explained. “I have to have some connection with the person in order to be able to help fill in the story.”

One such connection was with German filmmaker Berger, who made his first English-language film , Conclave , from a script by Peter Straughan, for which the latter won the Oscar for best adapted screenplay.

“I hadn’t made an English-language movie yet, and I was really looking for one,” Berger said. “I don’t care who writes the damn script as long as it feels personal, and Peter Straughan is one of the best writers in the world. His adaptation is much better than my adaptation would have been.”

Ross said her public funding experience at BBC Film and Film 4, where the combination of quality and purpose – the desire to reach an audience with things that matter – was key in making decisions, has never left her.

“Those muscles are very hard to lose. I wish I could lose them a bit. I wish I could say, ‘Oh, this is big and expansive and definitely commercial.’ It’s just not the place I start,” she admitted.

Ross said she loved that an idea like Slumdog Milli o naire can come from an odd place that nobody wants to finance it, that the distributor wants to drop it, and it makes more money than any other film and wins eight Oscars.

But she said she believes it is harder than ever to raise the funding for independent films, even for her.

“The business is much more nervous than when I was funding films. It’s true that just because you’ve made a film that’s worked doesn’t mean anybody will trust you to do another one.

“The public money that exists in the UK for film, for a lot of the films I produce, I couldn’t make without,” Ross noted. “ Conclave we made without the support of any of that funding other than tax credit but we make a lot of our films with BBC or Film4 investment, and sometimes the BFI as well.”

Those organisations are vital for producers trying to raise the money for projects by first-time filmmakers, she added.

“I’ve been working for such a long time that I think I have a habit of falling in love with things and believing in an idealistic way that it must be possible,” Ross said. “If I believe it, I must find a way of making it possible, which is probably mad, and it must mean that there are lots of projects on my [House] slate that may never happen but that I will keep on trying to make happen.”

Her next project is set to be with another German director, Nora Fingscheidt’s Unbeaten starring Ralph Fiennes as the renowned real-life horse trainer Henry Cecil, supported by BBC Film and Studiocanal.

Berger had presented Ross with Rome Film Fest’s Industry Achievement award – established to pay homage to personalities in the global film industry who, through their memorable careers, have left an indelible mark on the history of cinema – the previous evening at the opening-night gala.

“Come and work with us,” CNC president Gaëtan Bruel urges UK producers

{"type": "paragraph", "text": "自2021年品牌诞生以来，La Nuit parfum便不断尝试将古典音乐不单作为香水的商品名来引用，而是将乐曲的结构、故事以及情感的变化本身转化为气味。在本次的试香纸中，这一方法论进一步扩展到了视觉表现。通过从单一乐曲向“音乐→气味→摄影”的不同感官进行层层翻译，使闻香水的体验本身更加接近一件复合型的作品。", クラシック音楽を香りに編曲するフレグランスブランド、「La Nuit parfum（ラニュイ パルファン）」が、ブランド設立5周年を記念して発表した新作オードパルファン5種のムエットに、国内外の写真家、アーティストによる作品を採用した。香りを試すための消耗品として扱われることの多いムエットを、音楽、香り、写真という3つの表現をつなぐメディアとして展開する。

2026年の新作は、フランツ・シュミット《7つの封印の書》、シェーンベルク《グレの歌》《浄められた夜》、ベルリオーズ《幻想交響曲》、チャイコフスキー《くるみ割り人形》の5作品。それぞれの楽曲を世界的指揮者ファビオ・ルイージ、ドイツの調香師ヨシカ・クレー、フランスのスタジオFLAIRが嗅覚へと翻訳した。各30mL、1万9800円（税込）で、10月7日から伊勢丹新宿店サロン ド パルファン 2026で先行発売される。

今回、それぞれの香りに対応するムエット（試香紙）も独立したビジュアル作品として制作。《7つの封印の書》には在本彌生、《グレの歌》には柏田テツヲ、《幻想交響曲》には山谷佑介、《くるみ割り人形》にはmanimaniumを起用。そして《浄められた夜》には、フランスを拠点に活動する現代美術家Marie Gueydon de Dives（マリー・ゲドン・ド・ディヴ）の作品が採用された。

世界を旅する在本は終末から新世界が生まれる曲に合わせ、光が差す希望を感じさせる1枚。山谷は野湯を撮ったONSENシリーズから、サイケデリックな作品を提供。柏田はウードを使用した叙事詩的に楽曲に神話的な屋久島の森を撮った。manimaniumは代表作である「ケーキでエロ本作れるし」シリーズのような官能的なデザートを撮影。Marieはダークな曲と香りに合わせて夜の森のシリーズをペアリングしている。

La Nuit parfumは、2021年のブランド誕生以来、クラシック音楽を単に香水の商品名として引用するのではなく、楽曲の構造や物語、感情の推移そのものを香りへと置き換えることを試みてきた。今回のムエットでは、その方法論をさらに視覚表現へと拡張。ひとつの楽曲から「音楽→香り→写真」という異なる感覚への翻訳を重ねることで、香水を嗅ぐ体験そのものをひとつの複合的な作品へと近づけている。

article_text:
Jessica Lange teased to Rolling Stone that her retirement from acting is likely coming soon. The Oscar winner returned to film and television this year with the releases of “Long Day’s Journey into Night” and “ American Horror Story 13,” respectively, but that might be it for the 77-year-old icon.

“I actually feel like I’m coming to an end,” Lange answered when asked about what projects she still wants to tackle as an actor. “Maybe it’s not a bad way to end, that last film being ‘Long Day’s Journey Into Night’ and playing Mary Tyrone. There are a couple projects that have been in the works forever that may or may not happen. I don’t know. It doesn’t seem easy to get things made anymore. At least not the kind of films that interest me.”

Related Stories

'The Diplomat,' 'Nobody Wants This,' 'East of Eden' Among Series to Take Part in Netflix's 'FYSee: The Fall Edit' Awards Showcase (EXCLUSIVE)

Netflix, ‘Elite’ Star Ester Expósito and Locarno Winner Mar Coll Adapt ‘La Regenta,’ a ‘Fresh Female Perspective’ on a Big Spanish Classic (EXCLUSIVE)

And how does Lange want to be remembered when her retirement becomes official? “For some good parts. For some good films. For being an honest actor,” she said. “I’ve been incredibly lucky. I love acting, and I’ve had decades of being able to do it, which has been a joy for me. Difficult at times, balancing family and career and locations and dragging my kids here and there. But it all was a great adventure. I’m so grateful that [it] came my way.”

Lange started acting in 1976 with her film debut in “King Kong,” which won her the new star of the year award at the Golden Globes. Her career would go on to include four more Golden Globe wins from 16 nominations as well as a Tony award (for “Long Day’s Journey into Night” in 2016) and six Oscar nominations, with wins for “Tootsie” (best supporting actress) and “Blue Sky” (best actress). She’s also been nominated for nine Emmy awards, winning three times for “Grey Gardens” (lead actress in a miniseries or movie), “American Horror Story: Murder House” (lead actress in a miniseries or movie) and “American Horror Story: Coven” (lead actress in a miniseries or movie).

In recent years, Lange has slowed down her acting output. While her film adaptation of “Long Day’s Journey into Night” opened in theaters in September, it was actually shot in 2022. She’s only starred in two other movies in the last decade: 2016’s “Wild Oats” and 2022’s “Marlowe.”

article_text:
“Galerna,” a fiction feature from Mexico’s Tatiana Huezo , has snagged the top prize at Impulso Morelia, the pix-in-post industry section of the 10-day Morelia Film Festival , which wraps Oct. 25. The José Maria Riba Award, presented by Cinépolis Distribution and Profest 2026, bestows $14,740. (250,000 pesos) toward outstanding post-production needs and/or promotional activities.

Only her second fiction outing, following “Prayers for the Stolen,” Huezo first received critical acclaim for her documentaries, led by “Tempestad” and “The Tiniest Place,” both produced by Pimienta Films (“Roma”). “Galerna” recently won the coveted Egeda Platino Industria Award at the San Sebastian Festival where it participated in the festival’s WIP Latin America competition showcase.

The road movie follows two casting directors into the remote reaches of Mexico, where their search for natural actors for a sci-fi film becomes an unsettling journey into their own fears, biases and preconceptions.

Following close behind with a Special Mention from the panel and a post-production award in kind from Caffeine was “Homeboys,” a documentary by Alonso Garibay and Alejandro Bernal which centers on Roberto Hernández, “Mr. Lucky,” who was deported to a country he barely knew and who later founded a shelter for those with similar experiences. “Homeboys” also took home the Eugenio Polgovsky award of $5,340.83 (100,000 pesos), created in memory of the beloved filmmaker.

“Tatiana’s ‘Galerna’ represents a new exciting direction for one of the best filmmakers working today, and I’m certain it will be a watershed moment in Mexico cinema when it is finally released to the public. I couldn’t be more thrilled than it is being recognized with the top prize. This year’s selection was fantastic, and I’m sure we’ll see these films succeed with audiences and critics,” said Piano ’s Julio Chavezmontes, one of the jurors in the international panel.

“On a personal note, it was deeply moving to see the inaugural Eugenio Polgovsky award go to “Homeboys”. This is a film that shares Eugenio’s fearless humanism, and I have no doubt he would have championed it, if he was still with us today,” said Chavezmontes.

For fellow juror Mauricio Durán Ortega, president of National Film Industry Chamber, Canacine, “Impulso’s selection was outstanding, as always.”

“All the projects deserved support and having a film reach that stage is already a major achievement. The award makes a real difference in helping filmmakers complete their work. Since most projects are already in post-production, our recommendations focus on what can still be refined. This year, the decision was unanimous – ‘Galerna’ stood out so clearly that no further debate was needed.”

Post-production house Caffeine, selected “Galerna,” “All the Water in the World” and “Homeboys” to receive in-kind services valued at over $20,000 (387,000 pesos) in total.

For Caffeine CEO Adrian Geyer, all three “show the range of Mexican cinema right now.”

“Tatiana Huezo’s road movie takes us down paths that feel supernatural without ever becoming so, with images that tell so much they let us travel alongside the characters; Diego del Río and Diana Bracho’s ‘All the Water in the World’ dares to explore aging and family from a place Mexican cinema rarely goes, with an honesty that unsettles us because it confronts us, as viewers, with ourselves; and Alonso Garibay and Alejandro Bernal’s ‘Homeboys’ gives a voice, in their debut documentary, to people both countries have tried to forget.”

Fernanda Garduño of Estudios Splendor Omnia chose documentaries “Raká,” and “Katechon” as winners of its in-kind services at the studios’ facilities in Tepoztlán, Morelos, which are valid for two years.

“I chose Teresa Camou’s “Raká” for its sensitive direction, intimate storytelling and striking images. By letting its subjects speak for themselves without imposing judgments, the film offers a poetic view of alternative ways of life. Support for sound design will help bring its full potential to life.”

For Garduño, Javier Toscano’s “Katechon” stands out for its “compelling portrayal of hope as a disciplined way of life rather than a cliché. Despite some familiar documentary tropes, its exceptional archival footage and creative storytelling make it visually distinctive and deserving of the award to support its color grading and finalization.”

The 12 th Impulso Morelia unspooled Oct. 18-20 during the festival. Below are the prizewinners.

article_text:
坂出市在住の彫刻家・辻󠄀野榮一とイラストレーター・辻󠄀野由樹による「いきもの」をテーマにした二人展を開催します。

辻󠄀野榮一（1960～）は、「焦がす」という行為を、自身の表現技法の主な特徴としています。素材の個性を際立たせ、特徴的なマチエールを出現させるこの技法を用いて、自然の造形美を手本に、生命力あふれる木彫や焼絵の作品を創り出します。

辻󠄀野由樹（1964～）は、温かみのある作風で絵画や絵本を手掛け、挿絵や広告美術にも関わります。彼女が描くのは「ナンセンス」な世界です。すぐ近くにあるかもしれない、おかしくてへんてこないきものたちの世界を、ピュアで自由な視点で描きます。

２人はともに、無数の生命から形づくられる奇跡のようなこの世界の美しさを、デジタルツールではなく自分たちの手によって表現します。ぜひ、五感を使って、２人がそれぞれの手法で生み出すユニークないきもの達の数々をお楽しみください。

期 間： 令和８年１０月１０日（土）～令和８年１１月２９日（日）

場 所： 高松市塩江美術館 企画展示室

時 間： 午前９時～午後５時（入室は午後４時３０分まで）

観 覧 料： 一般３００円、大学生１５０円（常設展観覧料含む／団体は２０名以上２割引）

高校生以下及び６５歳以上の方、身体障害者手帳等の所持者、高松市キャンパスメンバーズ制度加盟大学等の学生は無料

＊１１月１４日（土）「塩江美術館の日」は無料

休 館 日 : 月曜日（１０月１２日（月・祝）、１１月２３日（月・祝）は開館、１０月１３日（火）、１１月２４日（火）は休館）

主 催： 高松市塩江美術館

article_text:
When Danielle Bensky first went to The Donald J Trump and Jeffrey Epstein Memorial Reading Room, she didn’t know what to expect.

“What happens if I walk in and survivors’ names are just plastered everywhere?” Bensky wondered about the reading room, a traveling exhibition of Epstein investigative files, first held in a New York City gallery this May. “I was a little worried in the beginning that this would be a form of exploitation for survivors.

“Instead, it was just so beautifully done.”

The reading room is meant to bring attention to Epstein’s crimes and law enforcement’s decades-long failure to act. The former financier, who counted numerous high-profile men among his associates, was arrested in 2019 for sexual abuse of teen girls but killed himself in jail.

While Ghislaine Maxwell was arrested and found guilty of luring teen girls into Epstein’s orbit, documents reveal that law enforcement officials were well aware of their crimes decades prior. Survivors have called for greater transparency and legal actions against any other participants in their sexual abuse.

Bensky also didn’t know what would happen when David Garrett, founder of event organizer the Institute for Primary Facts , floated an idea to make the exhibit more interactive. There was a cork board in the final room and Garrett told Bensky he was going to keep it there when this exhibition opened to the public, so visitors could leave notes.

“I was like, ‘Oh, that’s such a great idea,” said Bensky, who is among the Epstein survivors pushing for accountability and justice. “That’ll be so cool to see.”

About a week after the reading room officially opened, Bensky returned and saw “at least six or seven corkboards that were full and overflowing with notes”. There were notes with drawings and notes with abject sadness and “sometimes, it was pure rage”.

“Sometimes, it would be a note directly to a survivor. Sometimes it was a note directly to themselves, and it got everybody involved,” she said. “Even members of survivors’ families were leaving notes. It was just a really beautiful display of our democracy.”

Bensky said the notes have given her hope amid years of institutional failures.

“Being seen in this process has been pretty remarkable.” Visitors have written, “We’re here with you, we stand with you, and we believe you” – demonstrating the “really beautiful empathy that comes with every single note”, Bensky said.

“There have been days where I felt like I couldn’t really do much. I felt really debilitated,” Bensky said. “The reading room can be a lot when you’re walking through your trauma all day, and you’re meeting all kinds of people.

“But so many of us will just go and sit in the room with all the notes and read the notes, and it’s like, ‘Wow, what an extraordinary thing to actually be seen and be believed by so many people at this point.’”

Liz Stein, an Epstein survivor, expressed similar sentiments about the power of these notes.

“It started out with one bulletin board, and I will never forget seeing that one initial bulletin board and just really feeling like, ‘Oh my goodness, people are really reacting to that,’” Stein said. When the first reading room installation ended, these notes “took up the better part of the downstairs of the exhibit”.

“The love that people show us is overwhelming, and every time we do these events with the reading room, every single time, people hug us, they tell us what we mean to them, and a lot of times they’ll say, ‘But it doesn’t matter. I’m just someone you don’t know from somewhere you don’t live,’” Stein said.

“And it’s like, no, we might not know your individual names, but we feel the love.”

“This wall with the note cards is a really tangible visual representation of how much support we have, and that fuels us in a way that I don’t think people quite understand.”

Garrett said that the idea for a notes space came at the last minute. He thought that people might experience deep emotions from the exhibit and might feel the need for support.

So, organizers put up a cork board with information about the national suicide prevention hotline as well as resources for those experiencing gender-based violence. Without thinking about it too much, Garrett decided to leave some extra notecards and pens.

“We just put them out and said, “if you want to write a note to the survivors, you can do that,” he told the Guardian. “We didn’t think that we would need more than that two foot by three foot corkboard.”

“By the end of the first day, not only was the corkboard full, but [notes] were taped up all around the cork board.” After just one day, visitors had left about 300 cards.

For the next 10 days, the producer would buy more cork boards everyday. There were 30 by the time the reading room ended its initial exhibition. “Every surface on that basement downstairs was full of cork boards and full of cards.”

The reading room would come to have seven stops – New York City; Washington DC; Des Moines, Iowa; Columbus, Ohio; Detroit, Michigan; Dallas, Texas; and Fort Lauderdale, Florida – and a traveling bookmobile that made about two dozen stops. In total, visitors left approximately 12,500 or 13,000 notes, Garrett said.

The reading room kicked off several months before highly contentious midterm elections dealt Republicans numerous blows which, some commentators said, was due to voters rejecting Trump. The president and Maga Republicans have been saddled by his administration’s handling of the files since he took office.

The White House rejected criticism of Trump’s handling of the files.

“Just as President Trump has said, he’s been totally exonerated on anything relating to Epstein,” White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said.

“And by releasing thousands of pages of documents, cooperating with the House oversight committee’s subpoena request, signing the Epstein Files Transparency Act, and calling for more investigations into Epstein’s Democrat friends, President Trump has done more for Epstein’s victims than anyone before him.”

Trump’s DoJ rebuffed criticism of their handling of these files and condemned the reading room.

“This sham tour is traveling to politically competitive areas and shamefully using victims as political pawns,” a DoJ spokesperson said in a statement.

“The non-profit’s fundraising ploy, which often hosts candidates for office, is a disgrace. It’s thanks to this Department of Justice that they even have those files, released in compliance with the Epstein Files Transparency Act under the most transparent administration to date.”

The words from supporters, both in person and notes, have provided encouragement to keep pushing for justice in spite of institutional roadblocks, Stein said.

“Your courage is louder than the people who tried to silence you,” was among Stein’s favorite notes. Another, Stein recalled, said: “One of these girls could have been me or my friends.”

“Money and power should not dictate justice,” Stein said of another memorable note.

Bensky also recalled one particularly powerful message.

“There was one that was just so simple,” Bensky recalled. “I think it literally just said: ‘It wasn’t your fault.’”

article_text:
When “ Percy Jackson ” series stars Walker Scobell, Leah Sava Jeffries and Aryan Simhadri make the trek to Italy’s Lucca Comics and Games Festival in late October – to unveil unseen footage ahead of the Nov. 20 release of Season 3 of “Percy Jackson and the Olympians” – they will travel to a unique geek meet held within the 16th century walls of a medieval Tuscan town that is attended by more than 200,000 fans each year.

This massive event dedicated to fandom, cosplay and the whole world of comics, including movies and TV, is the biggest pop culture festival in Europe. Lucca in recent years has reached a level of relevance for Hollywood and the Asian industry that is second to none.

Related Stories

Disney+ Strikes Landmark Content Deal With U.K.'s Channel 4 That Streamer Says Is Among Its 'Most Significant' Globally

Variety speaks to Giovanni Cova, who is head of Milan-based entertainment marketing company QMI that leads programming of Lucca’s film and TV strand, about how the event is bolstering its status as an unmissable launching pad at a time when the role of traditional festivals as promotional vehicles is being questioned.

This year we are, of course, absolutely delighted to have Disney’s support and to serve as a key stop on a major promotional tour, in this case, for “Percy Jackson.” I believe that, in the grand scheme of things, this further confirms that Lucca has become an essential international stage to unveil major series released in the autumn season. In recent years, we have served as “a” — if not “the” — primary showcase for titles like “Stranger Things,” “Squid Game,” “Wednesday” and “The Lord of the Rings.” Lucca has firmly established itself as a constant presence on the global promotional circuit for studios and streaming platforms, which is something that gives us great satisfaction. The fact that such significant promotional events are taking place here in Europe, in Italy, and specifically in a city like Lucca is truly gratifying. Of course, we must thank the local offices of the major studios and streaming services. They have effectively communicated the importance of Lucca to the decision-makers back in Los Angeles.

Given the high profile of the guests who attend Lucca, the media exposure we generate is truly significant. Furthermore, the unique nature of the Lucca festival, the photo opportunities it provides, and the chance for talent to get up close and personal with their actual fans is, in my view, absolutely priceless. You can see this in the images from the launches of series or films in Lucca. They travel around the world because they are so distinctive. Very different from the typical red-carpet scene. Seeing the ancient Piazza San Michele packed with people, and witnessing those genuine encounters between the cast and the audience. That is the unique experience we offer to the entertainment world.

Well, it’s fantastic for us to have Frank Miller here. He loves Italy; he loves Lucca, and he’s returning for what I believe is the fourth or fifth time. We couldn’t be happier. Frank truly embodies the values of Lucca and the types of genre we love. We also have talents like Kore-eda [Hirokazu] who this year attended the Cannes Film Festival for one type of project [“Sheep in the Box”], but is then coming to Lucca for another [“Look Back”]. Then there’s Joe Manganiello, who, much like Frank, is a huge fan of Lucca. He embodies the festival’s spirit, spanning cinema, video games and tabletop games. He really represents the multimedia nature of Lucca.

Another crucial aspect of Lucca is that, beyond the screenings and the presence of talent, the festival offers the public a chance to truly engage with a property. To experience it firsthand. There are pavilions and live installations where the audience can immerse themselves in these worlds. We’ll have a “Harry Potter” experience, a K-pop-themed experience from Netflix, and a pavilion from Crunchyroll, which, in addition to hosting numerous premieres, allows fans to engage directly with its content. We’ll also see this with “Percy Jackson,” from Disney, as well as with “Dexter” for Paramount+. Ultimately, these installations, these immersive, interactive and event-driven experiences are just as significant as the presence of talent.

In my view, the main difference between Lucca and traditional festivals is that, at Lucca, there is no filter between the content, the talent and the audience. Traditional festivals are events where content is typically presented to industry professionals and the press, who then act as intermediaries, bringing that content to the general public. In Lucca, instead, film criticism is not part of the festival’s DNA. For Lucca, presenting content simply means bringing it directly to the fans. There is no mediation by industry insiders, critics or film journalists. And I say this without being judgmental. It is simply that we are not that type of festival. Consequently, we don’t have to worry about generating “bad press,” as that falls outside our scope and purpose. We simply provide studios with the opportunity to connect directly with the audience, whether through content or specific activations.

editorial_title_zh: 摄影师约尔根·阿克瑟尔瓦尔（Jörgen Axelvall）出版记录30年历程的回忆录《Art Rat》。并将举办出版纪念座谈会
editorial_excerpt_zh: 以东京为活动基地的摄影师约尔根·阿克瑟尔瓦尔（Jörgen Axelvall）出版了由摄影与文字组成的回忆录《Art Rat》。全书包含约3万7000字、共30章，通过散文与诗意的叙述，延伸了其作为摄影师创作的作品世界，是一本250页的著作。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "以东京为活动基地的摄影师约尔根·阿克瑟尔瓦尔（Jörgen Axelvall）出版了由摄影与文字组成的回忆录《Art Rat》。全书包含约3万7000字、共30章，通过散文与诗意的叙述，延伸了其作为摄影师创作的作品世界，是一本250页的著作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "阿克瑟尔瓦尔在《Art Rat》中回顾的是自己人生的30年。他将自己在纽约度过的15年与至今在东京度过的15年串联起来，以第一人称记述了1990年代至2000年代在纽约的记忆、感染HIV的经历、此后被诊断出4期癌症，以及与伴侣共同面对的种种艰难。尽管涉及严肃的经历，叙述中却不时穿插幽默，将个人记忆与围绕疾病的经验展开为一部节奏明快的纪实作品。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他于2019年开始写作。当时阿克瑟尔瓦尔认为，通过替代性的整体疗法（holistic therapy），其HIV病情得到了抑制。然而在2020年被诊断出癌症后，病情急剧恶化，面临生命危险。写作一度中断，在曾坚信的价值观动摇之中，他最终接受了科学治疗作为通往康复的道路。据称，在经历了4年的缓解期后重新提笔时，最初构想的故事及其意图也发生了巨大的变化。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本书的特征在于将文字与摄影并置的结构。在30个章节之间均设有2个跨页的影像页面，除照片外，还收录了诗句、警句、格言和诗歌等。所刊载的61幅照片涵盖了模拟胶片、即时成像胶片、宝丽来以及数码摄影等多种形式，均选自阿克瑟尔瓦尔历时30年积累的个人档案。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在《Art Rat》中，照片并非用于说明文字的图版。过去拍摄的影像与从当下回望过去写下的文字在同一时间轴上交织，从多重视角重新构筑了摄影师的个人历史。这也是一部通过镜头面对世界的阿克瑟尔瓦尔，将其创作实践延伸至“写作”这一行为的作品。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "疾病与康复、纽约与东京、过去的照片与当下的文字。《Art Rat》并未将30年的时光局限于一部线性的自传中，而是通过在不同时代的影像与文字之间穿梭，对自身生命进行重新编辑。该书作为限量200册的作者版于2026年7月出版。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "为纪念新书出版，9月12日将在涩谷的NONLECTURE books/arts举办题为“《Art Rat》是如何诞生的——用摄影与文字编织30年的记忆”的座谈会。阿克瑟尔瓦尔与负责本书设计的阿加·德·ロス·サント斯（Aga de los Santos）将出席，由ARTnews JAPAN主编名古摩耶担任主持人，共同讲述将30年的记忆通过摄影和文字编纂成书的幕后制作背景。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "出版纪念座谈会“《Art Rat》是如何诞生的——用摄影与文字编织30年的记忆” 日期：2026年9月12日（周六）16:00〜17:00 会场：NONLECTURE books/arts（涩谷） 出席者：约尔根·阿克瑟尔瓦尔、阿加·德·ロス·サント斯 主持人：名古摩耶（ARTnews JAPAN） 参与费：1,000日元＋1杯饮料费", "translated": true}]

article_text:
東京を拠点に活動する写真家ヨーガン・アクセルバル（Jörgen Axelvall）が、写真と言葉による回想録『Art Rat』を刊行した。約3万7000語、全30章からなる本書は、写真家として制作してきた作品世界を散文や詩的な記述によって拡張する、250ページの一冊だ。

『Art Rat』でアクセルバルが振り返るのは、自身の人生の30年。ニューヨークで過ごした15年間と、現在まで東京で過ごしてきた15年間をつなぎながら、1990年代から2000年代のニューヨークでの記憶、HIVへの感染、その後のステージ4の癌の診断、パートナーとともに直面した困難を一人称で綴っている。深刻な経験を扱いながらも、語りには時折ユーモアが差し込まれ、個人的な記憶と病をめぐる経験がテンポのあるノンフィクションとして展開される。

執筆を始めたのは2019年。当時アクセルバルは、代替的なホリスティック療法によってHIVが抑制されていると考えていた。しかし2020年に癌と診断されると病状は急速に悪化し、生命の危機に直面。執筆はいったん中断され、それまで信じていた価値観が揺らぐなかで、科学的治療を回復への道として受け入れることになる。4年間の寛解を経て執筆を再開したとき、当初構想していた物語とその意図もまた、大きく変化していたという。

本書を特徴づけるのが、文章と写真を並列させた構成だ。30章それぞれの間には見開き2ページのイメージページが設けられ、写真とともに詩句や警句、格言、詩などを収録。掲載される61点の写真は、アナログフィルム、インスタントフィルム、ポラロイド、デジタル写真と多岐にわたり、30年にわたって蓄積されたアクセルバル自身のアーカイブから選ばれている。

『Art Rat』において写真は、文章を説明するための図版ではない。過去に撮られた像と、現在から過去を振り返って書かれた言葉が同じ時間軸の上で交差することで、写真家の個人的な歴史を複数の視点から組み立て直していく。レンズを通して世界と向き合ってきたアクセルバルが、その実践を「書く」という行為へと拡張した作品でもある。

病と回復、ニューヨークと東京、過去の写真と現在の言葉。30年という時間を一つの直線的な自伝に閉じ込めるのではなく、異なる時代の像と言葉を行き来しながら、自らの生を再編集する『Art Rat』。200部限定の著者版として2026年7月に刊行された。

刊行を記念し、9月12日には渋谷のNONLECTURE books/artsでトークイベント「『Art Rat』ができるまで──写真と言葉で綴る30年の記憶」が開催される。アクセルバルと、本書のデザインを手がけたアガ・デ・ロス・サントスが登壇し、ARTnews JAPAN編集長の名古摩耶をモデレーターに、30年にわたる記憶を写真と言葉によって一冊の本へと編み上げた制作の背景を語る。

出版記念トーク「『Art Rat』ができるまで──写真と言葉で綴る30年の記憶」 日時：2026年9月12日（土）16:00〜17:00 会場：NONLECTURE books/arts（渋谷） 登壇者：ヨーガン・アクセルバル、アガ・デ・ロス・サントス モデレーター：名古摩耶（ARTnews JAPAN） 参加費：1,000円＋1ドリンク代

ハッシュタグは #豊臣兄弟

国衆に一揆をたきつけた罪で、成政（白洲迅さん）に切腹を命じた秀吉（池松壮亮さん）。二度と同じことが起きないようにと、全国に刀狩令を発する。

秀長（仲野太賀さん）が領民に、秀吉が建立する大仏の資材として戦道具の提供を促す一方、秀次（山田涼介さん）は力ずくで召し上げようとする。

そんな中、大名の中には秀吉の政策に不満を持つ者がいると知った秀長は、大和郡山城に家康（松下洸平さん）ら諸大名を招き、本音を聞き出そうと考える。

title_original: Day by Day: Peter Hujar’s Day
editorial_title_zh: 日复一日：彼得·胡亚的某一天
editorial_excerpt_zh: 生活中的肖像：伊拉·萨克斯的《彼得·胡亚的某一天》，一部关于这位著名摄影师的“非典型传记片”，在平凡中找到了魔力

"关于彼得·胡亚，我知道这样两三件事：他是一位摄影师，主要活跃于1970年代和80年代，作品常以纽约艺术家和作家的冷峻黑白肖像为主。他是一名男同性恋者。他于1987年因艾滋病相关肺炎去世，年仅53岁。这些事实在多大程度上构成了一幅准确的人生肖像？而任何肖像又能否真实地描绘一个无法追回的过去？这些问题驱动着伊拉·萨克斯的新片《彼得·胡亚的某一天》，这部“非典型传记片”将胡亚搬上银幕的方式，不是聚焦于他人生的大脉络，而是通过某一天斜向切入。影片暗示，生活的实质不仅在于事实记录中呈现的内容，也在于填满一个人分分秒秒和日日夜夜的那些琐碎之事。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这些细节源自影片的结构性构思，它直接改编自胡亚和他的朋友、作家琳达·罗森克兰茨在1974年12月某天的一次对话。作为一项最终未能实现的出书计划的一部分，罗森克兰茨架起一台录音机，请这位摄影师精确细致地讲述他前一天所做的一切。这次访谈延续了罗森克兰茨长期以来对日常生活的追问——她1968年的《谈话》一书，将她和朋友们逐字记录的真实对话变成了一部小说。她设想，日常生活是每个人都以为自己理解、却从未真正深入思考过的东西。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "尽管原始录音已经遗失，但这段对话的一份打印文字稿最近在胡亚的档案中被发现，并于2021年作为书籍出版。萨克斯将这段对话逐字搬入剧本（略有删减），由本·卫肖饰演胡亚，丽贝卡·豪尔饰演罗森克兰茨，并将他们的相遇安排在作家那间阳光充沛、绿意盎然的上曼哈顿公寓中。结果有点像一部室内剧，几乎完全由两个人交谈构成——大多是关于日常生活的琐碎之事，比如胡亚午睡时是否穿着衣服，以及外卖店排在他前面的那个人点了什么。这种处理方式的效果，不是缩小我们对什么构成一段人生的理解，而是扩展它。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "萨克斯克制住了切到胡亚所描述的那一天画面的冲动，始终紧守对话场景，即直接录在磁带上的那一刻。录音机的反复出现强调了这一叙事策略：卫肖和豪尔说出的每一个字都直接取自文字稿。然而，将艺术作品建立在现实之上，并不能保证真实，这一点胡亚比任何人都更清楚——他曾说过，“一张照片完全是虚构。”为了抵消对逐字来源的使用，影片刻意指涉自身的建构：开场是一个场记板的镜头，并在某一刻让一支吊杆麦克风闪入画面。演员们突然更换地点和服装，影片从厨房跳到卧室再跳到屋顶，即便他们的句子在剪辑之间仍不间断地继续。有几次，影片飞入想象的画面，仿佛突然唱起歌来：在莫扎特音乐伴奏下的插曲中，豪尔和卫肖摆出戏剧化的姿态，直视镜头。即便影片以其叙事构思的真实性主张将我们拉入其中，它也以这些花招与我们保持距离，提醒我们它（以及任何）纪录片式记录的残缺不全。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但影片并未止于这个镜头。相反，在余下的光线中，我们看到罗森克兰茨停下录音机，随后萨克斯切回胡贾尔，他的脸突然从黑暗中浮现。在这段档案录音渐渐消逝后的间隙里，胡贾尔发出一声漫长而疲惫的叹息，随后突然仰起头，仿佛在回应来自画框之外的某个信号。也许惠肖是在看围绕他正在拍摄的这部电影，又也许那是胡贾尔在环顾四周，终于讲完了自己的一天。无论哪种情况，某种既在影片之外、也在其素材之外的东西探了进来，打断了它的情境。忽然之间（他们真的一直在说话吗？），夜晚已经过去——黎明从背景中探出头来。影片指向画框之外，肯定了可能性：在某个地方，对彼得·胡贾尔来说，也许还会有另一天。", article_text:
Here are two or three things I know about Peter Hujar: he was a photographer, active primarily in the 1970s and ’80s, whose work often featured stark black-and-white portraits of artists and writers in New York. He was a gay man. He died, at just 53 years of age, in 1987 due to AIDS-related pneumonia. To what extent do facts like these compose an accurate portrait of a life? And can any portrait ever truthfully depict an irretrievable past? These questions animate Ira Sachs’s new film, Peter Hujar’s Day , a not-quite-biopic that brings Hujar onto the screen not by focusing on the broad strokes of his life, but by approaching them aslant through a single day. The stuff of life, the film suggests, is not just what appears in the factual record, but the banalities that fill a person’s minutes and days.

These details are drawn from the structural conceit of the film, which directly adapts just one single conversation Hujar and his friend, writer Linda Rosenkrantz, had on a December day in 1974. As part of a never-to-be-realized book project, Rosenkrantz had set up a tape recorder and asked the photographer to recount in precise detail everything he had done the previous day. The interview was a continuation of Rosenkrantz’s ongoing investment in interrogating the everyday—her 1968 book Talk had transformed verbatim real conversations with her friends into a novel. The everyday, she imagined, was something everyone assumed they understood yet never actually thought very deeply about.

Though the original recording was lost, a print transcript of the conversation was recently discovered in Hujar’s archives and published as a book in 2021. Sachs lifts the dialogue word for word into his screenplay (with minor cuts), casts Ben Whishaw as Hujar and Rebecca Hall as Rosenkrantz, and stages their encounter in the writer’s lush, sun-filled Upper Manhattan apartment. The result is something like a chamber drama, consisting almost entirely of two people talking—mostly about the banalities of daily life, like whether Hujar wore clothes during his nap and what the person in front of him in line at the take-out place ordered. The effect of this approach is not to narrow our sense of what makes up a life, but rather to expand it.

Sachs resists the impulse to cut away to images of the day Hujar describes, holding fast to the scene of the conversation, the moment directly inscribed onto the tape. Repeated shots of the tape recorder underline this narrative strategy: every word uttered by Whishaw and Hall is taken straight from the transcript. Yet basing a work of art in reality is no guarantee of truth, something Hujar knew better than anyone—he remarked once that “a photograph is a complete fiction.” Offsetting its use of the verbatim source, the film goes out of its way to reference its own construction, opening with a shot of a slate and including, in one moment, a boom mic flashing into frame. The actors abruptly change locations and outfits, as the film jump-cuts from the kitchen to the bedroom to the roof, even as their sentences continue unbroken across the edits. A few times, the film takes flight into imagined tableaus, as if breaking into song: interludes set to Mozart in which Hall and Whishaw pose theatrically and stare directly into the camera. Even as the film draws us in with the truth-claim of its narrative conceit, it keeps us at bay with these flourishes, reminding us of the incompleteness of its (and any) documentary record.

The recourse to fiction also gives the film a way of undercutting reality, circumventing the tragedy of Hujar’s death. If the specter of the AIDS epidemic loomed over the lives of gay men in the subsequent decade, linking them irrevocably to tragedy and death, Peter Hujar’s Day insists, instead, on the terms of life. There is no direct reference to death anywhere in this film, neither in the conversation nor in the contextual titles that appear at the beginning. Instead, the film’s carefully circumscribed everyday fashions a space of day-to-day living against the pervasive tendency, etched into the historical record, to render queer life as proximate to death.

Sachs also understands that the everyday is not outside of that record. There’s a mournful undercurrent to the film, one that rises increasingly to the surface as the day draws to a close. Darkness settles into the apartment, and Whishaw’s performance becomes heavy with wistfulness and lethargy. “I don’t feel good,” he laments about his smoking habit. In the film’s closing sequence, Sachs frames Whishaw and Hall exclusively in separate shots, creating a sudden distance between the two that’s jarring in a work that has so often presented their bodies close together. One moment of portraiture at the end of the sequence has Hujar looking straight at the camera, staring blankly, his face illuminated by the soft lamp beside him—before the light abruptly shuts off, leaving his features partially shrouded. It’s hard not to read this gesture as something like turning the lights out, a way to acknowledge death without ever explicitly rendering it on screen. A delicate visual elegy, then—a curtain drawn.

But the film does not end with this shot. Instead, in the remaining light, we see Rosenkrantz stop the tape, before Sachs cuts back to Hujar, his face suddenly emerging from the darkness. In this interstitial space after the archival recording trails off, Hujar lets out a long, fatigued sigh before suddenly craning his head upward, as if responding to a signal from beyond the frame. Maybe Whishaw is looking at the film being made around him, or maybe it’s Hujar looking around, finally done retelling his day. In either case, something outside of both the film and its source juts in and interrupts its situation. All of a sudden (have they been talking all this time?), the night is already past—dawn peeks out from the background. Gesturing toward what’s outside the frame, the film affirms possibility: somewhere out there, for Peter Hujar, another day might follow.
article_translation_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "我知道关于彼得·胡贾尔的两三件事:他是一位摄影师,主要活跃于1970年代和80年代,他的作品经常包含在纽约的艺术家和作家的坚硬黑白肖像,他是一位同性恋者,他死于1987年仅53岁,因艾滋病相关的肺炎,到什么程度这些事实构成一个准确的生命肖像? 任何肖像都可以真诚地描述一个不可逆转的过去? 这些问题动画伊拉萨克斯的新电影,彼得·胡贾尔的日子,一个不合适的生物,将胡贾尔带到屏幕上,而不是通过专注于他生命的广阔冲击,而是通过接近他们在一天内,生活的物品,这部电影提议,不仅仅是事实记录中出现的东西,而是一个人的几分钟和几天。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这些细节是从电影的结构概念中提取出来的,这直接适应了只有一个单一的对话,胡贾尔和他的朋友,作家林达·罗森克兰茨,在12月的一天在 1974 作为一个未实现的书项目的一部分,罗森克兰茨设置了一个录音带记录器,并要求摄影师详细记录他前一天所做的一切。 1968 《谈话》改变了真实的谈话她想象的日常,是每个人都认为他们理解的东西,但从来没有真正深思熟虑。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "虽然原创录制失去了,但最近在胡贾尔的档案中发现了对话的印刷翻译,并于2021年作为一本书出版,萨克斯将对话词为词提取到他的剧本中(有小切割),将本·威什瓦(Ben Whishaw)作为胡贾尔和雷贝卡·霍尔(Rebecca Hall)作为罗森克兰茨(Rosenkrantz),并在作者的温暖、充满阳光的上曼哈顿公寓中进行他们的会面。日常生活的平凡性,如胡贾尔是否在他的睡眠期间穿着衣服,以及他面前的人在接下来的位置上所命令的事情。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "萨克斯抵抗了对Hujar描述的那一天的图像的冲动,坚持到对话的场景,直接录制的时刻。 录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制录制电影走出自己的道路,参考自己的建筑,开启一个射击的滑板,并包括,在一个时刻,一个泡沫微闪闪在框架。 演员突然改变位置和服装,因为电影跳从厨房到卧室到天花板,即使他们的句子继续在编辑中无断。 几次,电影飞到想象的图像,好像破碎在歌曲: interludes设置到莫扎特,在那里Hall和Wishaw立场戏剧和观看直接到即使这部电影吸引了我们对其讲故事概念的真相声明,它也让我们与这些花朵相处,提醒我们它的(和任何)纪录片的不完整性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "使用虚构也给了电影一种破坏现实的方式,围绕着胡贾尔的死亡的悲剧,如果艾滋病疫情的频谱在接下来的十年里围绕着同性恋人的生活,无可逆转地将他们与悲剧和死亡联系起来,那么彼得胡贾尔的日子却坚持生活的条件。仔细地循环日常时尚,一个日常生活的空间,反对被历史记录的侵略性倾向,以使可爱的生活接近死亡。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "萨克斯也明白,日常生活不在记录之外,这部电影有一个可怕的下流,一部随着日子的关闭,越来越多地升到表面上,黑暗进入了公寓,威沙夫的表演变得沉重,有智慧和无情,“我感觉不舒服,”他抱怨他的吸烟习惯。这是在一份工作中漫步,经常把他们的身体聚集在一起。一瞬间的肖像在序列结束时,胡贾尔直观摄像头,看着白色,他的脸被他旁边的软灯照亮了 - 直到光突然关闭,让他的特征部分缩短。然后,一张窗帘,一张窗帘。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但電影並沒有結束這部拍攝,而在剩下的光中,我們看到羅森克蘭茨停止了帶,直到薩克斯切斷了回到胡格爾,他的臉突然從黑暗中出現。在這間互動空間中,在檔案錄音的軌道下,胡格爾放下了一個漫長的,疲倦的眼光,然後突然把他的頭向上,好像回應一個信號從超越框架。在任何情况下,电影和其来源之外的某些东西都聚集在一起,并中断了它的情况,突然的一切(他们一直在谈论这一切吗?),夜晚已经过去了,从背景上跳出,向外的框架转向,电影确认了可能:在某个地方外,为彼得·胡贾尔,另一个日子可能会跟随。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Cable and camera: selfies in 1970s Handsworth

Nearly 50 years ago in inner-city Birmingham, photographers Derek Bishton, Brian Homer and John Reardon set up an impromptu studio in the street and invited their neighbours along. With no camera phones in 1979, long cable releases gave participants the power to decide how they wished to be seen and represented. The project’s original aim was to counter negative media images of Handsworth and its people. Now, in collaboration with Dewi Lewis Publishing, a Kickstarter fund has been set up to bring them together in book form

"“造一头鲸鱼需要举全村之力，而我认为要从中活下来，需要一个非常出色的村庄。这确实是[制作过程中]最令人欣慰的部分之一，”达菲尔德在9月Deadline探班洛杉矶拉德福德制片厂的片场时说道，当时正在拍摄早期的一个水箱场景，艾布拉姆斯第一次与鲸鱼相遇。“这是一个如此新颖而独特的挑战，我觉得我们雇对了人，因为我们很多人每天都在绞尽脑汁，想办法怎么拍。”", "links": [{"text": "set of the movie at Radford Studios", "url": "https://deadline.com/2026/09/whalefall-production-california-producers-interview-1236528267/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "新西兰的维塔工作室制作了多个鲸鱼胃模型，而头部、喉部、食道和喉头则在加州建造，因为它们太大，无法按时运到片场。这个高12英尺、长18英尺的鲸鱼头由StudioArt & Technology制造。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/WHALEFALL-TF-4.jpg?w=300", "alt": "", "caption": "奥斯汀·艾布拉姆斯饰演杰伊·加德纳，出自20世纪影业的《鲸落》 20世纪影业", "credit": "Deadline · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“这是一个环环相扣的片场。我从未拍过一部电影，也无法想象拍一部每个部门在每一步都真的必须相互沟通的电影，”达菲尔德说。“就胃而言，我们的美术指导拉姆齐[艾弗里]必须想办法把它建起来，然后我们得想办法把摄影机放进去，但接着还得想办法打光，然后灯光又变成了生物荧光。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "视觉特效总监纪尧姆·罗什龙曾参与乔丹·皮尔的《不》，他布置了胃里的LED灯光，最终将其渲染成生物荧光，进而照亮杰伊所处的环境。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“有些颜色在LED灯下显示出来的颜色不一样。所以，我们的服装设计师必须根据LED灯会呈现的效果来设计奥斯汀的服装，”达菲尔德补充道。“所以我们会把氯丁橡胶样品带到新西兰——我们在那里建造了胃——在灯光下、靠着鲸鱼皮肤展示，看看会呈现什么颜色。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "拍摄期间，摄影机和镜头“不停地”损坏；剧组最终围绕摄影机唯一能放进狭窄空间的那个位置来构建场景，并从那个视角倒推拍摄。如果这还不够幽闭恐惧，艾布拉姆斯还面临额外的挑战：要在面罩和杰伊使用的潜水装备后面表演情绪。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我们重新设计了调节器，让它尽可能小，因为调节器本来就不是在水外佩戴的。然而，鲸鱼胃里的空气是有毒的。它不一定会杀死他，但里面充满甲烷和其他东西，会让他有点兴奋，”达菲尔德说。“所以我们重新设计了调节器，尽可能让他能做出嘴型。他在整部电影里确实会自言自语，或者和胃里的其他角色说话。这是一个很有挑战性的学习过程。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/WHALEFALL-TF-1.jpg?w=300", "alt": "", "caption": "奥斯汀·艾布拉姆斯饰演杰伊·加德纳 20世纪影业", "credit": "Deadline · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "影片创作中这些艰巨的方面，呼应了克劳斯写书的一贯方式；他如今已出版了30多本书。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我喜欢制造新问题，然后必须努力想出解决办法——我试着从一个不可能的[设定]开始，把我不了解的东西像跨栏一样扔到自己面前，”克劳斯在片场告诉Deadline。“所以我每次都得重新学习如何写一本书。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《鲸落》的灵感来自一段病毒式传播的视频，视频中一名皮划艇爱好者最终落入鲸鱼口中。克劳斯听说这段视频后，便与朋友们讨论这种事是否真的可能发生。他无法停止思考这件事。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在给作家朋友玛丽·罗奇——著有《吞咽：消化道历险记》（2013）——发了一封电子邮件，并与她推荐的3位鲸鱼专家通信后，克劳斯找到了这本书的“高概念”钩子，该书于2023年出版。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“抹香鲸极其聪明。它们是地球上最神秘的动物之一。关于它们的一切都很奇怪。它们真的感觉像外星生物。即使在充满类外星生物的深海中，鲸鱼也几乎感觉像是外星生物中的主宰。它们不是侵略者。它们是非常和平的动物。抹香鲸曾许多许多次被目睹帮助人类，比如帮助遇到麻烦的潜水员。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "从内到外体验一头鲸鱼，为《Whalefall》的故事增添了复杂的层次，甚至涉及故事核心的父子关系时也是如此。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“基本上，你怎么能通过它的内脏爱上一个角色？这确实很恶心，但我们有哪些方式可以爱上这只动物，因为奥斯汀处于如此独特的情境中，而且我觉得他的角色有些有趣之处，他非常喜爱动物和自然，”达菲尔德说。“区分他的角色和乔什的角色的一点是，乔什非常坚硬，奥斯汀非常柔软。但他们都热爱自然，所以给奥斯汀一些时刻，让他能够——用更好的说法来说——欣赏这个情境有多酷，同时又吓得魂飞魄散、几乎随时都觉得自己要死了——这也是创作的一部分。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "达菲尔德显然也有类似的敬畏。对他来说，胃部作为电影大部分场景的诀窍在于，在杰伊困境的幽闭感与脱离狭窄空间的喘息之间取得平衡。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“这有挑战性，原因有几个。其一，这是电影中很长的一段，他在胃里时发生了相当多的事情，但也要保持新鲜和有趣，这样30分钟后，人们不会只是说，‘好吧，我受够这个胃了，’”达菲尔德说。“[杰伊]确实有一些不同的小支线冒险。他在第二个胃里待了一段时间，那个胃在视觉上非常不同，然后也在鲸鱼的食道里。胃里还有不同的动物，他必须用麦基弗式的方法摆脱不同的问题，所以只是想办法在视觉上保持新鲜，而丹尼尔在书里老实说做了很多这方面的工作。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《Whalefall》执行制片人道格·梅里菲尔德的作品包括《自由威利》系列电影，他与达菲尔德、克劳斯和Imagine Entertainment的艾伦·曼德尔鲍姆一同强调，鲸鱼不是电影中的反派。最终是虎鲸攻击了杰伊的抹香鲸，提供了反派角色和电影高潮的催化剂。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“鲸鱼不是坏家伙。鲸鱼只是一只动物，在做它该做的事。鲸鱼对[杰伊]不感兴趣。它想抓一只鱿鱼，而奥斯汀挡了路，”达菲尔德说。“电影最终在乔什·布洛林和鲸鱼之间建立了非常直接的联系，而奥斯汀旅程的一部分就是与他电影开头就已死去的父亲和解。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/WHF-02141_R2.jpg?w=300", "alt": "", "caption": "左至右：奥斯汀·艾布拉姆斯饰杰伊·加德纳，乔什·布洛林饰米特·加德纳 20th Century Studios", "credit": "Deadline · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "吸引达菲尔德执导这部改编作品的书的主线之一是其核心的父子关系；探班时他自己的儿子4岁。在《Whalefall》中，米特和杰伊并不总是知道如何最好地相互沟通；海洋是他们找到共同点的地方。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“这本书的奇迹，也希望是电影的奇迹，在于当它结束时，你主要谈论的是那些关系，然后鲸鱼是第三或第四层构建，对于一部几乎完全设定在鲸鱼内部的电影来说，这感觉不可能，但[克劳斯]不知怎么做到了，”达菲尔德说。“随着年龄增长，你开始从不同视角看待事物。我想在我当爸爸之前，我可能会坚定地站在杰伊的视角，然后现在站在另一边、有了一个儿子——当然，我儿子刚满4岁，所以这和[杰伊]与[米特]之间的关系非常不同——[我]真的开始对布洛林的角色产生同情，并在某种程度上理解他。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "克劳斯在保守的爱荷华小镇长大，在构建米特和杰伊关系的张力时，他深入了个人经历。他的父亲是个猎人，不像米特那么极端，但仍然是这个角色的灵感来源。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我是[我成长之地]的产物，也就是说，我一直避免接受心理治疗。我是那种文化的产物，在人际事务上，你不表达自己，也不表露自己的感受，”克劳斯说。“米特在海洋方面是个非常情绪化的人，比如他会为那里的每一个生物拼尽全力。他会不惜一切代价保护海洋。但到了与儿子相处时，他完全不知所措。他与鲸鱼互动会比与儿子互动好得多。最终，米特在某种意义上变成了鲸鱼，而通过鲸鱼，他们能够进行那场对话。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "当杰伊对抗氮麻醉——潜水员体内某些气体对神经系统产生麻醉作用、导致一种亢奋状态的情况——以及鲸鱼胃里的甲烷时，他会闪现回忆，这些回忆帮助他拼凑出生存所需的信息。这些记忆往往涉及父亲传授的智慧之言，无论杰伊当时是否那样看待它们。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“真正的挑战在于，书里大概有50段闪回，不断来回跳跃。在电影里，[我们]必须把杰伊需要知道的所有信息从那些闪回中提取出来，想办法把它们压缩进少得多的闪回里，”克劳斯说。“那才是最大的挑战。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "一个小的创作细节进一步将米特与鲸鱼融合在一起，在克劳斯的书中，他们作为一个角色说话。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“鲸鱼的心脏在跳动，胃部对鲸鱼心跳的节拍作出反应。所以那是声音在操控胃部。里面有水，水也随之移动。然后，在这一切之上，为了展示它如何开始形成完整的循环，鲸鱼的心跳就是乔什·布洛林的心跳，”想出这个主意的达菲尔德解释道。“我们录下了乔什的心跳，然后我们的音效人员把它做成了正在播放的鲸鱼心跳。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/WHALEFALL-TF-2.jpg?w=300", "alt": "", "caption": "左至右：奥斯汀·艾布拉姆斯饰演杰伊·加德纳，乔什·布洛林饰演米特·加德纳 20世纪影业", "credit": "Deadline · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这个细节也与克劳斯的主题构想相契合。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“当我接触到鲸落这个概念时——也就是鲸鱼死亡后尸体沉入海底，其身体在分解过程中引发一波生命冲击，一代代生命从其遗骸中诞生——我觉得这非常动人，也很触动人心：当一头鲸鱼死去，或者我们认识和爱的某个人死去时，他们的死亡在某种意义上孕育了生命，对他们的记忆、他们的影响。它会延续下去，延续数代，甚至现在我说起它时都会起鸡皮疙瘩，这真是一个美好的想法，”克劳斯说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "有时候，需要被困在鲸鱼体内，才能获得一些视角。", "translated": true}]

I’ve never made a movie, and I can’t imagine ever making a movie where every single department really has to be talking to each other every step of the way,” Duffield said. “For the stomach, Ramsey [Avery] our production designer [had] to figure out how to build it, and then we [had] to figure out how to put cameras in it, but then also we had to figure out how to light it, and then the lights become bioluminescence."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Visual effects supervisor Guillaume Rocheron, who worked on Jordan Peele’s Nope , rigged the LED lighting in the stomach to eventually render as the bioluminescence that then helps illuminate Jay’s environment."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“Some colors do not show up the same color in LED lights. So, our costume designer had to build Austin’s costume around what the LEDs would show up with,” Duffield added. “So we would take neoprene samples to New Zealand, where we built the stomachs, to show them under the lights, against the whale skin, to see what colors show up.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Cameras and lenses were broken “nonstop” during filming; the crew ultimately constructed scenes around the one spot the camera could actually fit into the cramped space and worked backwards from that vantage point. If that weren’t claustrophobic enough, Abrams also faced the added challenge of emoting behind a facemask and the diving equipment Jay uses."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“We redesigned the regulator to make it as small as possible, because regulators are not really meant to be worn outside of water. He actually does talk throughout the movie to himself or to other characters in the stomach. That has been a challenging learning curve.”"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/WHALEFALL-TF-1.jpg?w=300", "alt": "", "caption": "Austin Abrams as Jay Gardiner 20th Century Studios", "credit": "Deadline · Film"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "These formidable aspects of the film’s creation echoe Kraus’ general approach to writing books; he now has 30-plus under his belt."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“I like to create new problems and have to fight through the solutions — I try to start with an impossible [conceit] where I just throw hurdles in front of me of things that I don’t know,” Kraus told Deadline on set. “So I have to relearn how to write a book every time.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The impetus for Whalefall came from a viral video in which a kayaker ended up in the mouth of a whale. Once Kraus heard about the clip, it spawned discussions with friends about whether it could actually happen. He could not stop thinking about it."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Following an email to author friend Mary Roach, author of Gulp: Adventures on the Alimentary Canal (2013), and correspondence with three whale experts she recommended, Kraus had found the “high concept” hook for the book, which hit shelves in 2023."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“I didn’t want to do it if it couldn’t really happen — being swallowed by a whale has been treated like a fable and Biblical stories forever. My interest was, could you do it scientifically accurately?” Kraus said. “And by the end of the day, I was all systems go. All the whale experts were super-excited to help, and they think about whales all day, but never in this context. We were off to the races.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Both Duffield and Kraus drew connections to the science fiction genre in different ways, with Kraus developing an interest in whales during the frontloaded research process for the book, which took about three months."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“I became more and more … obsessed, you might say, with whales,” he said. “There’s a lot of what I was doing with this biology of a whale, but I also unexpectedly started to get really enamored of whales as a being, as a force of nature."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“Sperm whales are extraordinarily intelligent. They’re one of the most mysterious animals on the planet. Everything about them is strange. They really feel like aliens. Even in the deep ocean, which is filled with alien-like creatures, the whales almost feel like a master alien. They’re not aggressors. They’re very peaceful animals. Sperm whales have been witnessed helping humans many, many times, like divers in trouble.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Experiencing a whale from the inside out adds complicated layers to Whalefall ‘s story, even when it comes to the father-son relationship at its heart."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“How do you fall in love with a character through its guts, basically? It’s definitely gross, but what are the ways that we can fall in love with this animal, because Austin is in such a unique situation, and I think there’s something interesting about his character, who is very fond of of animals and nature,” Duffield said. “One of the things that differentiates his character and Josh’s character is Josh is very hard and Austin’s very soft. But they both have this love of nature, and so giving Austin moments that he can really, for lack of a better way to put it, appreciate how cool the situation is — while also being scared sh*tless and thinking he’s going to die pretty much at any given moment — that was part of the craft of it, too.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Duffield evidently shared a similar awe. For him, the trick with the stomach being the setting for a majority of the movie was balancing the claustrophobic feeling of Jay’s plight with breaks from the cramped space."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“It’s challenging for a couple reasons. One, it’s such a long stretch of the movie, and quite a lot happens while he’s in in the stomach, but it was also about keeping it fresh and interesting so [that] after 30 minutes, people weren’t just like, ‘Alright, I’m sick of this stomach,’” Duffield said. “[Jay] does have different little side adventures. He spends some time in the second stomach, which is very visually different, and then in the esophagus of the whale as well. Different animals that are also in the stomachs, and different problems he has to MacGyver his way out of, so it’s just trying to figure out how to keep it fresh visually, which Daniel honestly just did a lot of in the book.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Whalefall executive prodcuer Doug Merrifield, whose credits include the Free Willy films, joined Duffield, Kraus and Imagine Entertainment’s Allen Mandelbaum in emphasizing that the whale is not the villain in the movie. It’s orcas that attack Jay’s sperm whale that ultimately provide the antagonists and the catalyst for the film’s climax."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“The whale is not a bad guy. The whale is just an animal that’s doing what it’s meant to be doing. The whale is not interested in [Jay]. It’s trying to get a squid, and Austin is in the way,” Duffield said. “The movie makes a very direct correlation, eventually, between Josh Brolin and and the whale, and part of Austin’s journey is making peace with his dad, who is dead at the start of the movie.”"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/WHF-02141_R2.jpg?w=300", "alt": "", "caption": "L-R: Austin Abrams as Jay Gardiner and Josh Brolin as Mitt Gardiner 20th Century Studios", "credit": "Deadline · Film"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "One of the main threads of the book that drew Duffield to directing the adaptation was the father-son relationship at its core; his own son was 4 at the time of the set visit. In Whalefall , Mitt and Jay didn’t always know how best to communicate with each other; the ocean is where they find common ground."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“The miracle of the book and hopefully of the movie is, when it ends, you primarily are talking about the relationships, and then the whale is third or fourth build, which for a movie that’s set almost entirely inside of a whale feels impossible, but somehow [Kraus] pulls it off,” Duffield said. “As you age up, you start viewing things from different perspectives. I think before I was a dad, I probably would have been firmly in Jay’s point of view, and then now being on the other side of it and having a son — granted, my son just turned 4, so it’s a very different than the relationship between [Jay] and [Mitt] — [I’m] really starting to feel for Brolin’s character, and understand him to some extent.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Kraus, who grew up in conservative small-town Iowa, leaned into the personal when it came to building the tension of Mitt and Jay’s relationship. His father was a hunter, not as extreme as Mitt, but still an inspiration for the character."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“I’m a product of [where I grew up], which is to say, I have avoided getting therapy. I’m a product of that culture where you don’t express yourself and you don’t show your feelings when it comes to interpersonal things,” Kraus said. “Mitt is a very emotional guy when it comes to the ocean, like he will fight tooth and nail for every living creature in there. He’ll do whatever it takes to protect the ocean. But when it comes to dealing with his son, he’s absolutely clueless. He would be much better at interacting with a whale than he would be his son. And ultimately, Mitt becomes the whale, in a sense, and through the whale, they are able to have the conversation.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "As Jay fights nitrogen narcosis — a condition in divers in which certain gases take on an anesthetic effect in the nervous system, resulting in a kind of high — and the methane in the whale’s stomach, he has flashbacks that help him piece together info he needs for his survival.
